title: Ford Fathom will be the cheapest American EV capable of powering a house

claims.claim: Ford announced two new EV chargers that will allow its forthcoming Fathom pickup truck to serve as a battery delivering power to the home or grid.

evidence.quote: Ford announced two new EV chargers today that will allow its forthcoming Fathom pickup truck to serve as a battery capable of delivering power to the home or grid.

claims.claim: Ford said the Fathom pickup truck will start at $28,350.

evidence.quote: Ford said the Fathom itself will start at $28,350.

claims.claim: The Fathom will be capable of delivering over 10 kW of power to a home.

evidence.quote: The Fathom will be capable of delivering “over 10 kW” to a home, Ford said.

claims.claim: The Home Power Station device will cost around $650, which is about 50% less than its first generation bidirectional charger.

evidence.quote: The automaker says it will cost around $650, about 50% less than its first generation bidirectional charger.

claims.claim: The Home Backup Power package will cost around $2,100, about 60% less than its first generation product.

evidence.quote: Ford says the package will cost around $2,100, about 60% less than its first generation product.

The other option, Home Backup Power, is a package that bundles the Home Power Station with a second device, the Home Backup Panel, to allow the Fathom to also power parts or all of a home when the power goes out. Ford says the package will cost around $2,100, about 60% less than its first generation product.

claims.claim: Installation costs for existing V2X chargers can run up to $10,000 depending on the electrical work needed.

evidence.quote: None of those prices include installation, which for existing V2X chargers can run up to $10,000, depending on how much electrical work needs to be done to prepare the home.

claims.claim: Payouts for Fathom owners who enroll in virtual power plants and sell electricity back to the grid can be upwards of $1,000 per year.

evidence.quote: Fathom owners who enroll and keep their truck plugged in can sell electricity back to the grid, often at a premium. Ford did not say how much Fathom owners can stand to make, but the payouts can be upwards of $1,000 per year, depending on the grid’s needs and the level of participation.
